texts: CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|~0.01, i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD momentum 0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.

Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.

SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Compute Δ with momentum; never treat momentum SGD as either automatically last or automatically strong.

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop at lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum averaging, zero-init square-avg inflates early steps up to ~10×) is noisy/unstable: vs choices with ≥3× smaller Δ it loses 12/27 at 3e-3 and 3/4 at 1e-3 (univariate); prefer Adam/AdamW at the same lr (Adam 3e-3 loses only 2/35) or RMSprop ≤3e-4. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs (nn.TransformerEncoderLayer default, no warmup) with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4, worst for d_model=128 or T≥1024; GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (high lr wins 12/17). (c) On MLP classification and Adam regression, lr 3e-3 is safe — take the larger Δ.

Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent.

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, spiral, and tabular when Δ<0.1): score each MLP = (number of LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest score; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then by greater depth. This picks 91/118 arch-only winners (univariate 28/31, multivariate 28/33). Pairwise more-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1). Mechanism: default init shrinks hidden RMS ~0.4-0.5× per unnormalized layer and output change per weight step ∝ feature magnitude, so LN + identity paths make an under-trained net move 2-3× faster. MLPs with zero LN win ≤12% unless depth=1.

Regression depth × residual (uni/multivariate MSE, any budget): a deeper residual MLP beats a shallower non-residual one 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide at similar params 70-32 (51-19 when lr·T<0.1); at equal depth extra width is a coin flip (5-5). Oscillatory/composite targets (sin(2πx)…, cos(2π sin…)) amplify the depth advantage: composition of 4-5 normalized residual blocks generates high-frequency curvature that 1-2 layer nets cannot reach within the budget. Non-residual deep stacks without LN are the exception: they attenuate signal and usually lose.

Activation × task: on MSE regression prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU. Pairwise vs other activations (same optimizer): LeakyReLU wins 51/77, ReLU 42/67, GELU 30/64, SiLU only 29/96. SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so stacked blocks attenuate signal/gradient and fit kinks/polynomials less precisely. The ranking flips for tabular classification once well-trained (see tabular rule): there GELU/SiLU win 16/16 vs ReLU-family. On XOR/spiral activation is a weak factor — decide by LN/residual/depth.

Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.

XOR and two-spiral classification (zero linear signal, chance CE=ln2≈0.693): loss stays on the chance plateau until weights move well beyond init, so (i) Δ is decisive — choices with Δ≲0.01 sit at 0.65-0.70 and are near-tied; (ii) among equal optimizers, deep RESIDUAL blocks with LN win: deeper+residual beats shallower plain 33-14 on classification, more-LN wins 20-5 on spiral (Δ≥0.01), deeper wins XOR at every budget (26-11). A 1-2 layer plain net rarely escapes the plateau in 256-512 steps. Spiral difficulty scales with turns: 1 turn best CE ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 turns ~0.45-0.6, 3 turns ~0.52-0.69 (nearly everything stuck → pick largest Δ).

Bigram LM architecture (same optimizer): a GRU LM beats a post-LN causal transformer in 17 of 18 pairs, at both weak and strong Δ. Mechanism: the task is a first-order lookup P(y|x_t); the GRU maps the current token straight to its output state and its tanh-bounded hidden state gives near-uniform initial logits (CE≈ln V), while the post-LN transformer feeds unit-RMS features to the head (logit std ~0.6, initial CE ~ln V+0.1-0.2) and must learn to ignore attention mixing. Among transformers prefer FEWER layers (1-2; fewer wins 40-23) and larger d_ff (26-13 when Δ≥0.05); d_model and total params are not predictive.

When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.

Bigram LM optimizer sweet spot: labels are sampled from P(y|x), so gradients carry irreducible noise and the achievable gain is only ~0.1-0.8 nats below ln V. Among choices with Δ≥0.1, prefer the one with Δ nearest ~0.3 (e.g. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop 3e-4 at T=512-1024, Adagrad 3e-3); treat Δ≥1 (lr≥1e-3 at T≥1024, lr 3e-3 at T≥512) as likely overshoot. Below Δ≈0.1 ordinary max-Δ still applies. This 'nearest 0.3' scoring picks 52/66 bigram optimizer/mixed winners vs 47/66 for plain max-Δ; adaptive-transformer winners are mostly lr 3e-4 (22/52). If all Δ<0.02 every LM stays ≈ln V and the GRU wins ties.

Dataset structure × depth (data-flip cue, same choices on different data): the deeper-is-better preference (under Δ<0.1) is strong for smooth/compositional targets — tabular smooth_additive (deeper 24-8), XOR with ≤4 input features (15-4), oscillatory univariate targets — but weak or absent when the rule is piecewise_boundary (5-6) or sparse_interaction (6-3) or XOR has 8-16 distractor features (11-7); there prefer the most-LN candidate regardless of depth. Spiral difficulty scales with turns (see XOR/spiral rule); polynomial/low-frequency univariate targets reach MSE 1e-4-1e-5, so stability (Adam over RMSprop at high lr) decides.

Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.

Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).

Δ≥0.5 (lr 3e-3 at T≥256, 1e-3 at T≥512): smaller d_model wins 5/6 and fewer layers only 3/10 — wide post-LN overshoots (cf. K1004b); order by d_model ascending, then layers (q_17f213: 32×3<32×4<64×1<64×2). Δ<0.02: all ≈ln V, deeper wins 10/17 (deeper-32 beat 64×1 in q_b66719). Winner-level 20/31 vs 18/31 for pooled 'fewer layers'. GRU still beats all (K1011).

Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger.

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop on MSE regression: only lr=3e-3 with T≤256 is risky — a coin flip vs choices with ≥3× smaller Δ (multivariate 5-5, univariate 6-7); prefer Adam/AdamW 3e-3 there (loses 2/35). RMSprop 1e-3 is NOT a ceiling (wins 15/15 multivariate, 7/12 univariate; q_b7e47f) and 3e-3 at T>256 wins 10/11 univariate. (b) Post-LN transformer LMs (nn.TransformerEncoderLayer default, no warmup) with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4, worst for d_model=128 or T≥1024; GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification and Adam regression: lr 3e-3 is safe — take the larger Δ.

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, spiral; tabular Δ<0.1 see K1009): score each MLP = (# LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest; break ties by activation on regression (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then greater depth (regression/XOR only — on TABULAR use LN count then FEWER layers: 20/22 vs 16/22). Picks 91/118 arch-only winners (univariate 28/31, multivariate 28/33). Pairwise more-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1); on regression LN outranks activation (30/41). Mechanism: each unnormalized layer shrinks hidden RMS ~0.5×. Exception: XOR ≥8 features at Δ≥0.05 (K1018).

TABULAR classification (synthetic_tabular, 1024 rows; smooth_additive/piecewise_boundary/sparse_interaction), MLPs sharing optimizer/lr/T; Δ per core rule (Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100). Lexicographic rule = 30/32 arch-only winners (old depth-based rule 26/32) + 4/4 same-optimizer subsets of mixed questions. Δ<0.1: (1) most LayerNorm blocks (41-4), (2) FEWER layers at equal LN count (shallower 12-4; 7-1 if residual equal; q_b556bd 2-layer beat 3-res/4-plain), (3) residual, (4) wider. Δ≥0.1: (1) GELU/SiLU over ReLU-family (16-0, even when deeper: q_f15cb3 5-layer SiLU beat 2-layer ReLU), (2) shallower (21-5), (3) fewer LN, (4) wider. Depth alone never helps.

Dataset structure × depth (data-flip cue): deeper-is-better (Δ<0.1) holds for XOR with ≤4 input features (15-4) and oscillatory univariate targets, but is weak when XOR has 8-16 distractor features (11-7; prefer most-LN, and at Δ≥0.05 GELU/SiLU decides — K1018). TABULAR: raw deeper-wins counts (smooth_additive 24-8) are a LayerNorm-count confound — at equal LN count the SHALLOWER MLP wins in every rule family (smooth_additive 7-2, piecewise 6-2, sparse_interaction 4-1, both Δ regimes); rank tabular by LN count then fewer layers (K1009). Polynomial/low-frequency univariate targets reach MSE 1e-4-1e-5, so stability (Adam over RMSprop at high lr) decides.

Tie-breaks differ by task: REGRESSION → activation (ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU), then greater depth; CLASSIFICATION (XOR/spiral/tabular) → WIDER, then SHALLOWER, not deeper (at equal score wider wins 17/22 pairs, shallower 16/23; arch-only Δ<0.1 picks 36/48 vs 32/48 with deeper). Arch-only hits: univariate 28/31, multivariate 27/33. Pairwise more-LN beats less-LN 61-11 (multivariate), 57-12 (univariate), 41-4 (tabular Δ<0.1). Exceptions: tabular Δ≥0.1 (K1009), XOR ≥8 features Δ≥0.03 (K1018), spirals ≥1.5 turns (depth floor rule).

Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive/piecewise/sparse_interaction): when shared Δ≥0.1 (Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100), the boundary is learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower 21-5, less-LN 15-5, smooth 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the LN rule holds (more LN+residual 42-6); 'deeper wins 35-17' is only because deeper nets carry more LN — at equal LN+residual pick WIDER then SHALLOWER (18/22 arch-only); at Δ<0.03 ReLU-family edges GELU/SiLU (20/30). Cutoff 0.1 fits best (26/32). XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.

A 1-2 layer plain net rarely escapes the plateau in 256-512 steps. Spiral best CE by turns: 1 turn ~0.001-0.03, 2-2.5 ~0.45-0.6, 3 ~0.50-0.69 — only ≥3-layer LN'd nets get below ~0.6 there, so depth+LN can beat ~8× more Δ (spiral depth-floor rule).

XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 pure-noise distractors) once moderately trained (shared Δ≥0.03; Adagrad Δ=2·lr·√T, e.g. Adagrad 1e-3 at T=256 → 0.032; Adam-family lr·T): tabular-style reversal — GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU 6/6 same-optimizer pairs, more-LN wins only 3/10, so pick the smooth-activation, wider, shallower net even with fewer LN (q_e914b6: 2-layer SiLU w192 1 LN CE 0.11 beat 5-layer 3-LN 0.17; q_b11fea: 3-layer GELU w256 won, 4-layer 3-LN LeakyReLU only 3rd, 5-layer ReLU last). With ≤4 features keep deeper/more-LN (7/7, 6/7 pairs); at Δ<0.02 the LN rule holds for all XOR (more-LN 6/8). Larger Δ still wins on XOR (6/7 pairs).

Two-spiral DEPTH FLOOR (≥1.5 turns; strongest at 2.5-3 turns): 1-2 hidden-layer MLPs stay near chance — at 2.5-3 turns median test CE 0.62 even with Δ≥0.1 (n=9), 0.68 at Δ 0.02-0.1 — while ≥3-layer nets with ≥2 LN blocks reach 0.50-0.59 at Δ≥0.02 (deep-LN beats shallow 6/6 pairs; at 1.5-2.5 turns, Δ 0.02-0.1: median 0.53 vs 0.67). So at ≥2.5 turns a deep LN'd net with Δ≥0.02 beats a 1-2 layer net even with ~8× more Δ (q_526f1b: 5-layer 3-LN plain Adagrad 1e-3 Δ0.032 beat 2-layer 1-LN residual AdamW 1e-3 Δ0.256). Below Δ≈0.01 all stay ~0.65-0.70 → max Δ. Shallow nets are fine only at ≤2 turns with Δ≥0.1. On spirals residual outweighs extra LN (6/8 pairs).

SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, momentum MSE regression 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. Largest Δ wins ~85% of optimizer-only and 83% (109/131) of mixed questions. A ≥3.5× Δ edge beats architecture (83/92 pairs); within ~3× architecture often decides — for mixed MLP questions use Δ×(1+#LN+residual) (K1012). Architecture-only: use architecture rules.

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr=3e-3 on MSE regression: vs a rival whose Δ is within 4× (e.g. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop 1e-3) it loses 9/10 pairs (q_c9b0f8, q_96a6ac, q_eb01b0, q_d6fe9e); vs ≥4× smaller Δ it wins 10/16 at T≤256 and 11/12 at T>256. Adam/AdamW 3e-3 is safe (loses 2/35); RMSprop 1e-3 is NOT a ceiling (wins 15/15 multivariate). (b) Post-LN transformer LMs (no warmup) with Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr≥1e-3 lose 14/25 to lr 1e-4-3e-4, worst for d_model=128 or T≥1024; GRU LMs tolerate 1e-3-3e-3 (12/17). (c) MLP classification and Adam regression: lr 3e-3 is safe — take the larger Δ.

MLP architecture default (regression, XOR, spiral; tabular Δ<0.1 see K1009): score = (# LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual; pick the highest. Ties on regression: activation tier ReLU = LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU (beats deeper worse tier 7/10), then greater depth within a tier (q_1f993c: 3-block ReLU beat 1-block LeakyReLU, while 3-block GELU lost to it). Picks 91/118 arch-only winners; more-LN beats less-LN 61-11 multivariate, 57-12 univariate. Mechanism: each unnormalized layer shrinks hidden RMS ~0.5×. Hidden LN does NOT erase spiral radius (q_9a80f8: 2-LN CE 0.56 beat plain 0.63/0.67). Residual vs one extra LN: coin flip (22/48). Exception: XOR ≥8 features, Δ≥0.05 (K1018).

Bigram LM architecture (same optimizer): a GRU LM beats a post-LN causal transformer in 20/21 corpus same-optimizer pairs (Adam/AdamW/RMSprop/Adagrad, plain SGD) and in q_17f213, q_b66719, q_bc0028 — rank the GRU first. Mechanism: first-order lookup P(y|x_t); the GRU maps the current token directly and its tanh-bounded state gives near-uniform initial logits (CE≈ln V), while the post-LN transformer feeds unit-RMS features to the head (initial CE ~ln V+0.1-0.2). EXCEPTION, SGD momentum 0.9: the GRU edge vanishes — q_8e4be7 (lr 1e-3, T=1024): d64 1-layer transformer beat the 1-layer GRU and the 2-layer GRU ranked LAST (n=1). Transformer shape: K1017.

Mixed questions (MLP; optimizer AND architecture differ): score = Δ × (1 + #LayerNorm blocks + 1 if residual), Δ per core rule; pick/rank by score. Corpus mixed winners 114.5/131 vs 109 for plain max-Δ (spiral 15 vs 13.5/16, univariate 28 vs 24.5/33, multivariate 28 vs 27/33, tabular 31 vs 30.5/33; XOR 12.5 vs 13.5/16 — on XOR use plain Δ). Pairwise, higher-Δ net with worse arch: Δ ratio ≤1.5× → better arch wins 13/19; ~3× → toss-up (higher Δ 22/37); ≥3.5× → higher Δ 83/92. Δ saturates once both ≳0.3. Rankings: near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture.
